# G2.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/g2-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/g2-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects product listing data from G2.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape G2 Company Data and Reviews](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-g2-company-data-and-reviews)
- **Code:** [`g2.py`](g2.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Review pages](results/reviews.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json) · [Alternatives pages](results/alternatives.json)

## What it scrapes

- G2 search pages for company listing data
- G2 review pages for company reviews data
- G2 alternative pages for company alternatives data

## Functions

- `scrape_search(url, max_scrape_pages=None)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape company listings from search pages
- `scrape_reviews(url, max_review_pages=None)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape company reviews from G2 review pages
- `scrape_alternatives(product, alternatives='')` → `Dict`: scrape product alternatives from G2 alternative pages

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import g2


async def main():
    search = await g2.scrape_search(
        url="https://www.g2.com/search?query=Infrastructure",
        max_scrape_pages=3,
    )
    reviews = await g2.scrape_reviews(
        url="https://www.g2.com/products/digitalocean/reviews",
        max_review_pages=3,
    )
    alternatives = await g2.scrape_alternatives(product="digitalocean")


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/reviews.json`](results/reviews.json): `author`, `review`
- [`results/search.json`](results/search.json): `name`, `link`, `image`, `rate`, `reviewsNumber`, `description`, `categories`
- [`results/alternatives.json`](results/alternatives.json): `name`, `link`, `ranking`, `numberOfReviews`, `rate`, `description`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`g2.py`](g2.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/g2-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_review_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`, `test_alternative_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
